frameworks.name: Anthropic Agent Skills structure
frameworks.summary: The published Agent Skills format: a folder with a SKILL.md entrypoint (YAML frontmatter name+description, markdown body) plus optional bundled resources, loaded via three-level progressive disclosure.

elements.name: SKILL.md entrypoint
elements.description: The skill is a directory with SKILL.md at its root.
elements.criteria: SKILL.md exists at the folder root.

elements.name: name frontmatter
elements.description: Required identifier, lowercase kebab-case.
elements.criteria: frontmatter has `name`, <=64 chars.

elements.name: description frontmatter
elements.description: Required; states what the skill does and when to use it (trigger cues, third person). The only part always in context.
elements.criteria: frontmatter has `description`, <=1024 chars.

elements.name: Progressive disclosure
elements.description: Three levels: metadata always in context; SKILL.md body loaded on trigger; bundled files read only as needed.
elements.criteria: Detail is pushed out of SKILL.md into bundled files rather than inlined.

elements.name: references/ resources
elements.description: Reference documents the agent reads as needed (level 3).
elements.criteria: references/ directory present with files.

elements.name: scripts/ resources
elements.description: Executable helpers for deterministic operations.
elements.criteria: scripts/ directory present with files.

elements.name: assets/ resources
elements.description: Templates and files used in the skill's output.
elements.criteria: assets/ directory present with files.

elements.name: Concise SKILL.md body
elements.description: Keep the body lean (guideline: under ~500 lines); move depth to references.
elements.criteria: SKILL.md is <=500 lines.

elements.name: Scripts for deterministic work
elements.description: Operations that must be exact ship as scripts instead of freehand generation.
elements.criteria: Deterministic steps (rendering, API calls, transforms) are backed by scripts/.

frameworks.name: Claude Code subagent schema
frameworks.summary: The subagent persona format: one markdown file whose frontmatter (name, description, tools, model) configures dispatch and whose body is the persona's system prompt.

elements.name: name frontmatter
elements.description: Required dispatch identifier.
elements.criteria: frontmatter has `name`.

elements.name: description frontmatter
elements.description: Required; the delegation trigger the main loop matches against.
elements.criteria: frontmatter has `description`.

elements.name: tools allowlist
elements.description: Least-privilege tool set for the persona.
elements.criteria: frontmatter has `tools`.

elements.name: model tier
elements.description: Persona pinned to a model/effort tier appropriate to its work.
elements.criteria: frontmatter has `model`.

elements.name: system-prompt body
elements.description: The markdown body is the persona's system prompt.
elements.criteria: non-empty body below the frontmatter.

elements.name: single responsibility
elements.description: One persona does one job; scope creep splits into a new persona.
elements.criteria: The body describes one coherent role, not several.

frameworks.name: hsb3 skill archetypes
frameworks.summary: Internal working taxonomy of what a skill fundamentally IS, derived from the shipped catalog. Not mutually exclusive; assess a primary archetype per skill. Candidate status: revise as the catalog grows or if Anthropic publishes a canonical set.

elements.name: Workflow / procedure
elements.description: Encodes a repeatable multi-step procedure the agent executes end to end (e.g. handoff, private-fork, board-triage).
elements.criteria: Body is dominated by ordered steps/protocol the agent performs.

elements.name: Domain expertise pack
elements.description: Teaches the agent a domain, tool, or API it would otherwise guess at (e.g. obsidian-*, opencode-expertise, mermaid).
elements.criteria: Body is dominated by reference knowledge, not procedure.

elements.name: Deliverable producer
elements.description: Produces a recurring artifact to a house standard (e.g. comms, pptx-themes, readme-value-and-proof).
elements.criteria: Output is a named artifact with format/quality rules.

elements.name: Guardrail / override
elements.description: Pins defaults or overrides behavior another surface would get wrong (e.g. house palette rules overriding a base skill).
elements.criteria: Body states precedence ('this skill wins') or bans defaults.

elements.name: Orchestration / delegation
elements.description: Structures how work is split across agents (e.g. foreman).
elements.criteria: Body is about dispatching/verifying other agents.

elements.name: Scaffold / auditor
elements.description: Stands up or audits repo/project structure against a documented standard (e.g. mise-en-place-scaffold, repo-compliance-audit).
elements.criteria: Body maps a standard onto a repo and creates/checks conformance.

frameworks.name: SKILL.md section taxonomy
frameworks.summary: The recurring section types observed across SKILL.md bodies; used to analyze composition (which sections a skill carries) and as a checklist when authoring new ones.

elements.name: Purpose / overview
elements.description: Opening statement of what the skill accomplishes.
elements.criteria: First section states the goal in 1-3 sentences.

elements.name: Trigger / when to use
elements.description: Beyond frontmatter: explicit in-body invocation and skip conditions.
elements.criteria: A section enumerates use/skip cases.

elements.name: Prerequisites
elements.description: CLIs, env state, or MCP servers that must exist first.
elements.criteria: A section lists dependencies before the workflow.

elements.name: Workflow steps
elements.description: Ordered procedure the agent follows.
elements.criteria: Numbered or staged steps present.

elements.name: Reference pointers
elements.description: Links into references/ or external docs for depth.
elements.criteria: Body points at bundled or external references.

elements.name: Examples
elements.description: Worked input/output or command examples.
elements.criteria: At least one concrete example block.

elements.name: Anti-patterns / pitfalls
elements.description: What NOT to do; known failure modes.
elements.criteria: A pitfalls/anti-pattern/common-mistakes section exists.

elements.name: Output format contract
elements.description: Exact shape of the deliverable the skill produces.
elements.criteria: A section specifies the output's structure.

elements.name: Integration partners
elements.description: Co-homed hooks/skills/agents this skill is load-bearing with.
elements.criteria: Body names sibling components and the shared contract.

frameworks.name: Hook directory layout
frameworks.summary: The ratified hook-dir layout enforced by scripts/check_hook_layout.py: each hook is a directory `hooks/<name>/` whose handler is `hook.py` (legacy flat `.sh` handlers and the old `hooks-handlers/` tree are banned), plus the stdlib-only rule from primitives-core/README.md ('hooks/<name>/ ... Claude-Code-only; stdlib-only (no pip/npm deps)').

elements.name: hook.py entrypoint
elements.description: The hook's handler lives at `hook.py` inside its own `<name>/` directory (ratified layout).
elements.criteria: hook.py exists in the hook's directory.

elements.name: Python-only handler
elements.description: No legacy `.sh` handler — check_hook_layout.py bans `.sh` files anywhere under a hook.
elements.criteria: No `.sh` file present in the hook's file inventory.

elements.name: stdlib-only imports
elements.description: The handler ships zero third-party dependencies (Python 3 stdlib only) — primitives-core/README.md's hook row.
elements.criteria: hook.py's top-level imports resolve to the Python stdlib only.

elements.name: config co-located
elements.description: Optional `config.json`/`hook.json` sits beside `hook.py` in the same directory.
elements.criteria: config.json or hook.json present in the hook's directory (optional).

frameworks.name: dotfiles-agents roster entry schema
frameworks.summary: This repo's manifest schema (primitives-core.yaml): id/type/source/shelf/origin/disposition/targets/plugins/requires, with origin:sourced and origin:vendored requiring upstream+ref. Enforced by scripts/check_roster.py.

elements.name: shelf
elements.description: core vs toggle shelving.
elements.criteria: Roster entry carries shelf.

elements.name: origin provenance
elements.description: authored vs sourced vs vendored is immutable; sourced and vendored require non-null upstream+ref.
elements.criteria: origin:sourced and origin:vendored entries have upstream and ref.

elements.name: disposition
elements.description: qualified | grandfathered-pending-use | demoted | untriaged | orphaned.
elements.criteria: Roster entry carries disposition.

elements.name: plugin membership
elements.description: Which bundles ship the primitive (plugins: []).
elements.criteria: Roster entry lists its bundles.

elements.name: requires capabilities
elements.description: Capability words {hooks, local-mcp, hosted-mcp} + cli:/env: dependency declarations.
elements.criteria: Dependencies declared in requires, not prose-only.

frameworks.name: hsb3 jobs-to-be-done taxonomy
frameworks.summary: The jobs Henry's agent work needs done, at deliverable altitude and spanning all work (software, exec/comms, research, knowledge-tooling, meta). Elements are solution-agnostic outcomes; W9 maps every extender to the jobs it serves so coverage gaps and overlaps become queries. Authored 2026-07-20 (EDB-13).

elements.name: Orient in an unfamiliar codebase
elements.description: When facing a system I don't know, get a reliable map of where things live and how they fit before acting.
elements.criteria: Serves this job if it helps an agent locate, inventory, or explain an unfamiliar codebase or system before changes are made.

elements.name: Research an open question into a cited answer
elements.description: When the answer lives outside the repo, gather multiple sources, verify them, and synthesize a cited result.
elements.criteria: Serves if it drives external information-gathering with source-grounding or fact verification.

elements.name: Consult domain expertise on demand
elements.description: When working in a specific technology, get its patterns and pitfalls in-session instead of guessing.
elements.criteria: Serves if its primary value is teaching or reference knowledge of a domain, tool, or API.

elements.name: Plan a piece of work
elements.description: Turn a goal into a sequenced, scoped, source-grounded plan before building.
elements.criteria: Serves if it produces an actionable plan or decomposition of work not yet built.

elements.name: Implement a bounded change
elements.description: Build a specified feature or fix within an owned file scope against acceptance criteria.
elements.criteria: Serves if it writes or edits product code to satisfy a defined change.

elements.name: Improve existing code without changing behavior
elements.description: Refactor, simplify, or tidy working code while preserving its behavior.
elements.criteria: Serves if it restructures existing code for quality without adding features.

elements.name: Apply one change across many sites
elements.description: Perform a single mechanical transformation across a large surface, with verification.
elements.criteria: Serves if it drives a repeated or bulk transform across many files or repos.

elements.name: Review a change for defects before it lands
elements.description: Find correctness, security, or quality defects in a diff before it merges.
elements.criteria: Serves if it inspects a change or diff and reports defects or risks.

elements.name: Verify a change actually works
elements.description: Drive the real system and observe the change behaving as intended.
elements.criteria: Serves if it exercises the running system to confirm behavior, beyond static checks.

elements.name: Delegate a large job across agents
elements.description: Decompose a big task, fan it out to agents, and reconcile the results.
elements.criteria: Serves if it structures multi-agent decomposition, dispatch, or reconciliation.

elements.name: Maintain project continuity across sessions
elements.description: Capture load-bearing state so a fresh or cold session can pick up the work.
elements.criteria: Serves if it externalizes session state for pickup or handoff.

elements.name: Manage a backlog or project board
elements.description: Triage, prioritize, sequence, and gate the work items.
elements.criteria: Serves if it operates or triages an issue or project backlog.

elements.name: Produce a stakeholder briefing
elements.description: Deliver a status or readout communication for a human audience.
elements.criteria: Serves if its output is a briefing, status, or readout artifact.

elements.name: Produce a slide deck
elements.description: Deliver a themed slide presentation.
elements.criteria: Serves if its output is a presentation or slide deck.

elements.name: Produce a diagram or architecture visual
elements.description: Deliver a structural, architecture, or flow visual.
elements.criteria: Serves if its output is a diagram (flowchart, ERD, architecture, sketch).

elements.name: Produce a data visualization
elements.description: Deliver a chart or data-driven visual.
elements.criteria: Serves if its output is a chart, plot, or dashboard from data.

elements.name: Produce a README or project pitch
elements.description: Deliver a README or pitch that communicates a project to its users.
elements.criteria: Serves if its output is user-facing project documentation or a pitch.

elements.name: Enforce and scaffold repo standards
elements.description: Audit or scaffold a repo against a documented meta-structure standard.
elements.criteria: Serves if it checks or creates repo or project structure against a standard.

elements.name: Govern external or OSS code
elements.description: Bring in and steward third-party code (fork, mirror, divergence tracking).
elements.criteria: Serves if it manages inbound external or OSS code and its governance.

elements.name: Get owner decision or sign-off
elements.description: Surface a batch of decisions to the owner for approval, outside chat.
elements.criteria: Serves if it collects owner decisions or approvals as a workflow.

elements.name: Author, evaluate, or curate an agent extender
elements.description: Build, judge, or curate a skill, agent, or hook and prove it earns its place.
elements.criteria: Serves if it creates, evaluates, or curates agent extenders themselves.

elements.name: Configure the agent harness
elements.description: Set up settings, hooks, keybindings, or permissions of the agent environment.
elements.criteria: Serves if it configures the harness or runtime (settings, hooks, keybindings, permissions).

elements.name: Integrate a personal-knowledge system
elements.description: Build or automate integrations for a knowledge tool such as an Obsidian vault or plugins.
elements.criteria: Serves if it builds or automates integration with a personal-knowledge system.

elements.name: Operate a browser or external UI
elements.description: Drive a browser or external UI to complete a task the CLI cannot.
elements.criteria: Serves if it automates a browser or GUI to accomplish work.

frameworks.name: SkillOpt skill-optimization methodology
frameworks.summary: Microsoft SkillOpt: treats a skill document as trainable state and improves it via scored rollouts against a task set with a machine-checkable reward, keeping an edit only when the candidate strictly beats the current skill on a held-out split. Cheap-model-native (openai_compatible backend -> Ollama/OpenRouter/local). Adopted as the quantitative eval+improvement methodology (W8/M5/M6). MIT.

elements.name: Scored rollout
elements.description: Evaluate a skill by running it as the system prompt/skill over a task set and scoring each rollout with a checkable reward (hard = exact-match 0/1, soft = partial 0-1).
elements.criteria: Eval scores a skill against a task set with a per-item reward, not by vibes.

elements.name: Validation-gated edit
elements.description: Accept a proposed skill edit only if the candidate STRICTLY beats the current skill on a held-out selection split; otherwise revert.
elements.criteria: Improvements are gated on a held-out score delta, never asserted.

elements.name: Authored benchmark required
elements.description: There is no generic 'grade my skill' - you author a task set plus a scorer (the reward IS the rubric) per skill/job.
elements.criteria: Each evaluated skill has an authored task set with a machine-checkable reward.

elements.name: Cheap-model substrate
elements.description: Runs against any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama/OpenRouter/vLLM/local); target and optimizer roles configured independently, so evals are cheap.
elements.criteria: Eval runs on inexpensive/free models via an openai-compatible endpoint.

elements.name: Transcript-mined improvement (Sleep)
elements.description: skillopt_sleep harvests real Claude Code/Codex transcripts, mines checkable tasks, and gate-improves the skill offline with human-in-the-loop adopt.
elements.criteria: Improvement can be sourced from real usage transcripts, gated before adoption.

frameworks.name: ClosedLoop judges + CaseScore rubric pattern
frameworks.summary: LLM-as-judge conformance pattern: each quality dimension is a judge prompt file carrying a deterministic rubric (severity table -> numeric formula -> threshold -> worked examples) that emits a strict CaseScore verdict; lightweight {id, input, expected_outcome} eval cases; a self-learning loop that persists validated patterns and injects them into future runs. Adopted as the qualitative conformance-judging pattern (borrowed onto our assessments). Apache-2.0.

elements.name: Judge-as-prompt with embedded rubric
elements.description: Each quality dimension is one LLM judge defined by a prompt file carrying a deterministic rubric: severity table, numeric scoring formula, threshold, and worked pass/fail/error examples.
elements.criteria: A conformance judge carries an explicit reproducible rubric, not vibes.

elements.name: CaseScore verdict contract
elements.description: A judge emits a strict verdict {final_status: pass/fail/error, metrics:[{name, threshold, score, justification}]}; the error state is excluded from aggregates so a crashed judge does not tank the grade.
elements.criteria: Verdicts are a validated schema with a first-class error state.

elements.name: Lightweight eval case
elements.description: An eval case is {id, input, expected_outcome} (JSONL) plus a 1-5 multi-dimension rubric - the cheapest hand-authorable golden set.
elements.criteria: Eval cases are small, declarative, and hand-authorable.

elements.name: Self-learning feedback loop
elements.description: Capture learnings (decision-tree gated) -> dedup/validate -> persist with deterministic success rates from an outcomes log -> inject top-N relevant patterns into future agent runs via a hook; citation-verified anti-gaming.
elements.criteria: Improvements are captured, validated deterministically, and fed back into future runs.
